video_title: Why GraphQL Exists: Client-Driven Data Shaping
core_insight: GraphQL inverts control of data shaping from server to client, solving over-fetching and under-fetching at the cost of server complexity and caching.

scenes.voice: Why does a single API need to serve web, mobile, and partners all at once?
scenes.visual: Three devices - web, mobile, partner portal - all hitting same backend, with different data needs highlighted.

scenes.voice: With REST, the server decides the shape. Mobile asks for id and name, gets email, profile, orders too. That's over-fetching.
scenes.visual: REST response box showing user object with many fields, mobile client only using two, rest crossed out.

scenes.voice: Or you need user plus orders items price. That's three round trips. Under-fetching.
New field needed? Version the API or duplicate endpoints. Frontend is coupled to backend release cycles.
scenes.visual: Version labels v1, v2 stacking up next to endpoint list.

scenes.voice: The real constraint is data shaping, not CRUD. Producers and consumers evolve at different speeds, and network is expensive.
scenes.visual: Two timelines: backend release slow, frontend iteration fast, with network cost icon.

scenes.voice: GraphQL inverts control. One endpoint, one schema. Client declares exactly what it needs in a single request. Server validates and runs only those resolvers.
scenes.visual: Client sends query box to /graphql, schema routes to resolvers, returns shaped response.
scenes.mermaid:
flowchart LR
    Client -->|POST /graphql { query }| Gateway
    Gateway --> Schema
    Schema --> ResolverA[Resolver]
    Schema --> ResolverB[Resolver]
    ResolverA --> Service1[(Service)]
    ResolverB --> Service2[(Service)]

scenes.voice: You gain frontend autonomy and fewer round trips. You pay with server complexity. Caching is hard because one URL with a POST body. N+1 queries can explode without DataLoader and cost limits.
scenes.visual: Scale icon up for autonomy, down for caching. N+1 diagram with many small DB calls.

scenes.voice: Use GraphQL when many heterogeneous clients need different shapes and UI moves fast. Avoid it when you need simple HTTP caching and service-to-service efficiency.
scenes.visual: Decision split: many clients + rapid UI -> GraphQL, public stable + CDN -> REST.

mental_model: Think of an API as a data shaping problem. REST pre-shapes responses for the server. GraphQL lets the client shape the response, trading server simplicity for client autonomy.
final_takeaway: GraphQL solves client-driven data shaping, not CRUD. One endpoint gives autonomy, but you must architect for cost control.
